explanation: Wanting Russians to look more European, he shaved some nobles himself in 1698. Later, bearded men paid a yearly tax and carried a token to prove it.

claims.text: Peter the Great, tsar from 1682 to 1725, imposed a tax on men who kept their beards.
In 1698 Peter the Great personally cut off the beards of some nobles.
Peter wanted Russian nobles to adopt European fashions.
Men who paid the beard tax received a token as proof of payment.
